correctness.rationale: PASS: Inspected frozen RESULT.md and verify_euler_fairness.py. In Eulerian support every degree is even, so first-group EF1 for a vertex with x_v incident selected goods is exactly 2x_v>=d_v. Component double-counting gives minimum ceil(|E(H)|/2), and alternating edge colors along an Euler circuit achieve this bound even with odd circuit length; moving extra edges to first group preserves EF1. This proves min |X|=(m+r)/2, minimum imbalance r, and after h neutral goods the optimal parity-constrained gap max((m+h) mod 2, r-h). With 2-regular support the discarded edge set is a matching; count optimal assignments by two perfect matchings of even cycles and length-many maximum matchings of odd cycles. Exponential formula for labeled undirected cycles yields EGFs E(z), O(z), D(z); parity-extracted singularity transfer gives C*n^(-1/4) even and C/4*n^(-1/4)*log n odd. Independently enumerated two disjoint triangles: 9 minimum EF1 allocations with first-group size 4, not balanced without h>=1; source verifier code inspected but its logged 741 and 4058 counts not represented as independent execution.

limitations: Exactly two fixed nonempty groups; all second-group agents indifferent; first-group degrees even, binary valued edges, no loops; random asymptotic uniformly labeled simple 2-regular only.
